topics.title: Attributes
topics.short: Six attributes from 0 to 100: Strength, Agility, Endurance, Intellect, Creativity and Perception. Jobs, crafting and the field all read them.
topics.long:
Every survivor has six **attributes**, each from 0 to 100: Strength, Agility, Endurance, Intellect, Creativity and Perception. Each job weighs a few of them: Woodcutting uses Strength and Endurance, Crafting uses Intellect and Creativity, Guard duty leans on Perception. See [[jobs_output]] for how they turn into output.

## How they grow

- Working trains the attributes the job weighs, a little every hour on shift. Gains shrink as a value nears 100.
- Children grow towards an aptitude inherited from their parents. Hungry hours do not count, so malnourished children grow up weaker (see [[children]]).

## In the field

- **Agility**: movement range, initiative, dodge and stealth (+0.3 stealth per point above 50).
- **Perception**: sight, detection (+0.5 per point above 50) and aim.
- **Strength**: carry capacity (10 kg plus 0.3 kg per point) and melee damage.
- **Intellect**: hacking chance and research speed.

## Tips

- Put people where their strongest attributes count: a high-Perception survivor makes a good guard and scout.

topics.title: Skills
topics.short: Thirteen skills from 0 to 100, from Woodcutting to Drone Piloting. They grow by doing the work, studying, or using them in the field.
topics.long:
Skills are what a survivor has learned: Woodcutting, Mining, Crafting, Tailoring, Electronics, Medicine, Firearms, Melee, Cooking, Farming, Hacking, Drone Piloting and Mechanics. Each runs from 0 to 100.

## How they grow

- **Work**: every hour on shift trains the job's skill. Some jobs train a side skill too: Electronics Lab work grows Hacking and Drone Piloting, Guard duty grows Melee, Hunting grows Farming.
- **Study**: classes at the Town Hall, Electronics Lab or Garage (see [[study_perks]]).
- **The field**: hacking, flying drones, salvaging and treating wounds train their skills, and the gains come home.
- Gains shrink as a skill nears 100. Children learn twice as fast.

## What they do

- Skill is part of job output (see [[jobs_output]]).
- The best worker's skill sets the quality of what a building makes (see [[crafting]]).
- Some recipes need a minimum skill. If nobody has it, workers **practise** instead of idling, and the order starts once someone is good enough.

## Tips

- Keep one person on a skill rather than rotating: the first points come fastest.

topics.title: Jobs and output
topics.short: How much a survivor makes per hour: the building's base rate times their attributes and skill, tool, health, age, mood, perks and food buffs.
topics.long:
Each worker's output is the building's base rate multiplied by a chain of factors. The breakdown below shows the live numbers for the selected survivor.

## The factors

- **Performance**: the weighted average of the job's attributes and skill. Even an untrained worker makes 25% of the full rate; a perfect one makes 100%.
- **Building level**: higher levels multiply output.
- **Tool**: a good tool adds up to the job's tool bonus (as much as +50%).
- **Health and body**: the body parts the job uses (an injured or missing arm hurts a woodcutter), times a vitality factor from ×0.5 at 0 HP to ×1 at full health.
- **Conditions and pain**: fever, sickness and bad injuries cost output (see [[infection]], [[injuries]]).
- **Age**: children work at half rate.
- **Mood**: from ×0.8 at mood 0 to ×1 at 100 (see [[mood]]).
- **Perks and cybernetics**: bonuses for this job.
- **Food buffs**: Well Fed ×1.08, Hungry ×0.85 and others (see [[food_buffs]]).

Per day, that rate counts only the hours on shift (see [[shifts]]).

## Tips

- Fix the biggest factor first: healing an arm or a good meal often beats a building upgrade.

topics.title: Output per day
topics.short: What each staffed building makes in a day on the current schedule, including night shifts and weather.
topics.long:
The colony's production is the sum of every worker's output (see [[jobs_output]]) over the hours they actually work. The breakdown below lists each staffed building's output per day, best first.

## What changes it

- **Shifts**: day-shift hours count fully; a Night Shift adds more hours at reduced output (see [[night_shift]]).
- **Weather**: rain, storms and dust slow outdoor work; the Greenhouse and indoor workshops do not care (see [[weather]]).
- **Damage**: a building hit by lightning, or damaged in a raid, works at half rate until repaired.
- **Crops**: farms and lodges bring in whole harvests once a crop has grown, so their output arrives in steps (see [[food]]).

## Tips

- Compare this list with what you use: if wood piles up and scrap runs short, move a worker.
- A building with fewer workers than slots is the cheapest boost there is.

topics.title: Day and night shifts
topics.short: Adults work 06:00 to 20:00 and sleep 22:00 to 06:00; children work 07:00 to 19:00. Missed sleep makes people tired.
topics.long:
The colony runs on a clock. Dawn is at 05:00, day at 07:00, dusk at 18:00 and night at 20:00.

## The schedule

- **Day shift**: adults work 06:00 to 20:00. Children work 07:00 to 19:00 and go to bed first.
- **Sleep**: adults sleep 22:00 to 06:00, children 19:00 to 07:00. Sleep in a bed (or a Med Bay cot) restores mood and a little health.
- **Evenings**: off work between dusk and bedtime, people sit at the Campfire for a mood lift. A hot meal after dusk adds a little more.

## Tired

Working through sleep hours builds **sleep debt**. At 4 hours of debt a survivor is **tired**: −15% output and a slow mood drain until they sleep it off.

## Tips

- Research, study and Med Bay care also follow the day shift.
- For more hours from a building, use a [[night_shift]], but watch for tired workers.

topics.title: Night shift
topics.short: Let a building keep working after dark at 70% output. Adults only, it costs mood, and outdoor sites need a Floodlight or level 2.
topics.long:
Switch on **Night Shift** in a building's panel and its adult workers carry on outside the day shift.

## The rules

- Output at night is ×0.7 of the day rate. A powered Floodlight adds +15% (see [[power]]).
- Only adults work nights; children always keep to the day shift.
- The building must be lit: indoor buildings always are; an outdoor site needs **level 2** or a **Floodlight** (10 wood, 5 scrap).
- Night work costs mood every hour and eats into sleep, so a standing night crew will usually be tired (−15% more).

## Side effects

- Night shifts are noise: they draw Husk raids (see [[raids]]).
- Guards on the night watch count as night workers too (see [[defenses]]).

## Tips

- Use it in bursts, for a stock you need now, rather than every night.
- Keep an eye on [[mood]]: low mood costs output on the day shift too.

topics.title: Mood
topics.short: Mood runs from 0 to 100. Low mood costs up to 20% output. Sleep, evenings by the fire and good meals lift it; grief, night work and storms drag it down.
topics.long:
Every survivor has a mood from 0 to 100. It starts at 100 and drifts back up slowly on its own.

## Why it matters

Job output and medic care are multiplied by mood: ×0.8 at 0, ×1 at 100 (see [[jobs_output]]). A survivor's [[humanity]] can cap how high mood may go.

## Up

- A night's sleep, evenings by the Campfire, a hot supper after dusk.
- Good dishes and the Comfort Food buff (see [[food_buffs]]).
- A repelled raid.

## Down

- Grief: a partner's death costs 50, a parent's or child's 25, a break-up 20.
- Night shifts and being tired (see [[shifts]]).
- Thunderstorms, fog and dust storms (see [[weather]]).
- A bland or repetitive diet, food poisoning, painkiller dependency.
- A lost raid.

## Tips

- After a death, give the family an easy few days: grief costs output on top of the lost worker.

topics.title: Housing and beds
topics.short: Everyone needs a bed. A newcomer without one has a few days' grace before they leave. Babies are only conceived when a bed is free.
topics.long:
Beds come from housing: a **Shelter** holds 6, 8 or 12 by level; a **House** (Town Hall 2) holds 10, 14 or 20.

## How homes work

- People keep their home. Newcomers move in with their partner or parents if there is room.
- A newborn or recruit with no bed starts a **grace timer** of a few days. It pauses while they are away on an expedition.
- When it runs out, an adult leaves. A homeless child leaves with a parent who is at home, which ends that parent's couple; with no parent at home, passing travelers take the child in.
- A couple only conceives when a bed is free for the baby (see [[family]]).
- Sleeping in a bed restores mood and health (see [[shifts]]).

## Tips

- Build a bed ahead of a birth or a rescue mission, not after.
- Recruits from expeditions come home without a bed.

topics.title: Couples and family
topics.short: Single adults at home grow closer every hour, faster when they share work or a home. At 100 they become a couple and may have children.
topics.long:
Every pair of single adults at home gains affinity each hour: a base amount, more if they work at the same building, more if they share a home, and more the more alike their attributes are.

## Couples

- At 100 affinity the closest ready pair becomes a couple.
- You can **encourage** a pair (×3 as fast), **discourage** them (no gain; it splits a couple) or reset them.

## Babies

- A couple who are both at home may conceive: a regular check with a 35% chance, when a bed is free and the stores hold at least 2 food per person.
- Pregnancy lasts a few days. A pregnant survivor stays home from expeditions.
- The baby's aptitude comes from the parents' average, give or take a little. See [[children]].

## Losses

A death costs the partner 50 mood and parents or children 25; a break-up costs 20. A detached cyborg strains their partner (see [[humanity]]).

## Tips

- Pairing two workers at the same building grows both affinity and output.

topics.title: Children
topics.short: Infants grow into children and children into adults in a few weeks. Children eat less, do light jobs at half rate and learn twice as fast.
topics.long:
Babies are born as **infants**, become **children** a few days later, and come of age about two weeks after that. The age shown in years is their share of the way to adulthood.

## What children do

- Infants cannot work and eat about half what an adult eats.
- Children can work Farming, Scrap Sorting, Crafting, Tailoring, Cooking and Distilling, at half output.
- They train twice as fast and earn more XP, so they grow into whatever they do.
- Children and infants are fed before adults.
- They never go on expeditions, stay in during dust storms and can be sheltered during raids.

## Growing up

Each fed hour moves a child's attributes towards their inherited aptitude, faster on good nutrition. Hungry hours do not count, so malnourished children grow up weaker (see [[food]]).

## Tips

- Put a child at the job you want them to be good at as an adult.

topics.title: XP, perks and study
topics.short: Work and missions earn XP; each level gives a perk point. Classes at the Town Hall, Electronics Lab and Garage teach skills and perks.
topics.long:
## XP and levels

Survivors earn XP for every hour of work, each finished batch, classes, and every mission (more for dangerous zones and for skill gained in the field). Each level gives **one perk point**, up to level 20.

## Perks

Perks sit in disciplines (Tech, Drones, Combat, Survival, Medic and others) with requirements: skills, attributes, other perks, a building level. Some are locked until you know a technique schematic (see [[schematics]]). Open a survivor's Perks tab to spend points.

## Study

- **Town Hall** teaches the colony skills; the **Electronics Lab** Electronics, Hacking and Drone Piloting (and the Tech and Drones perks); the **Garage** Mechanics. More students fit at higher levels.
- Alone, a student reaches skill 20; a **field manual** raises that cap.
- A **mentor** at least 5 points ahead doubles the pace and teaches up to their own level, at most two students each.
- A perk can be learned from a mentor who has it, without spending a point.
- Students and mentors leave their jobs while in class.

topics.title: Controls
topics.short: Space pauses, 1/2/3 sets the speed, B builds, F places defenses, E plans an expedition. In the field Space ends your turn.
topics.long:
## Everywhere

- **Esc**: pause menu or back. **F1**: help, every topic, searchable. **F3**: frame-time graph.

## Colony

- **Space**: pause and resume time. **1 / 2 / 3**: normal, 2× and 4× speed.
- **B**: build menu. **F**: place defenses. **E**: expedition planner. **I**: items and schematics. **P**: power overlay.
- **G**: garage. **M**: world map. **Y**: radio.
- **Tab**: next survivor. **Q / R**: turn the camera.

## Expedition planner

- **1–5**: jump to a step. **Tab / Shift+Tab**: next or previous step. **Enter**: next step, or launch on Review.

## Field

- **Space** or **Enter**: end turn.
- **1–9**: your orders in the order they are listed: attacks first, then items.
- **Tab**: select your next unit. **Home**: back to the unit whose turn it is. **Backspace** or right-click: cancel aiming.
- **O / B / L**: [[overwatch|overwatch, brace, lookout]].
- **F**: take all loot. **I**: salvage. **X**: extract. **C**: carry a downed ally. **R**: load loot into the vehicle.
- **H**: hack. **K**: deploy or recall the scout drone. **Shift+R**: the drone's role order. **Shift+I**: ferry a cargo drone's load out.

## Dialogue

- **Space** or **Enter**: next line.

The full list is in **Settings → Controls**.

topics.title: Construction
topics.short: Placing a building makes a construction site. Builders haul its materials over and put in work; it is done when both are in. Level 1 is a quick shed, upgrades take days.
topics.long:
Placing a building (or ordering an upgrade) makes a **construction site**. Its materials leave the stockpile at once, so you can only place what you can afford.

## How a site gets built

- **Builders** you assign (see [[builders]]) and idle people who lend a hand do the work, on the day shift.
- First they **haul** the materials from the stockpile to the site (see [[hauling]]). Work can never run ahead of what has been hauled.
- Then they put in **work**: each level has a build work amount. When the work is done and everything is on site, the building stands.

## Upgrades

- An upgrade takes much longer than a new level-1 building (see [[upgrade_time]]).
- **The building keeps working at its old level** while it is upgraded: its workers, output and beds carry on.

## Weather and raids

- Rain slows building, a thunderstorm more; a **dust storm stops it**.
- Raiders can knock a site back. An unfinished building stands as a frame (low cover) and later as walls in a defense battle.

## Controls

- **Pause** stops a site. **Priority** says where idle hands go first (Low: assigned builders only). **Cancel** gives back what was not hauled and most of what was.
- Builders keep the work schedule. An upgrade of a lit building can run a **Night shift**; a new building's site is dark.

topics.title: Builders
topics.short: Builders are people you put on a site with its "+" slot. Strength, Endurance, a little Intellect and Creativity and the Construction skill set their pace; idle people help at half pace.
topics.long:
Put someone on a site with a "+" builder slot. They leave their job or guard post for it, and become idle again when the building is done.

## Their pace

- Builders use the **Construction** job: Strength and Endurance most, some Intellect and Creativity, and the **Construction** skill, which grows by building (see [[skills]]).
- Tools, health, mood, conditions and food count as for any job (see [[jobs_output]]). The **Engineer** perk adds 15%, **Pack Mule** 10%.
- A fresh adult puts in about half a work unit an hour; a trained builder more.
- **Children** can build, at the child rate.

## Helpers

- Survivors with nothing to do (no job, post, site, bed, class or research) **lend a hand** at half pace, at the site with the highest priority that has room.
- Set a site to **Low** priority to keep idle people off it (for example to keep them on raid repairs).

## How many

- Each level says how many builders a site takes at once (2 for level 1, 3 for level 2, 4 for level 3).

topics.title: Hauling
topics.short: Builders first carry a site's materials from the stockpile, about 30 units an hour each. Work never runs ahead of what is on site.
topics.long:
A site's materials leave the stockpile when you place it, but they still have to be **carried over**. Builders haul about **30 units an hour** each (less when hurt, half for children).

- Builders keep the hauled share a little ahead of the work, then build, then haul the next load. You can see them walk to the Town Hall and back carrying loads.
- **Work can never pass the share of materials on site**: a site with nothing hauled cannot rise.
- The site panel shows each material as hauled / needed.
- **Cancel** gives back everything not hauled yet, and most of what was hauled.

topics.title: Build and upgrade time
topics.short: Level 1 is a quick, cheap shed: an hour or two with two builders. Level 2 takes about one to two days of one builder, level 3 three to five.
topics.long:
Each level has its own **build work**:

- **Level 1** is a simple shed: about an hour or two with two builders for a farm or a woodcutter, a few hours for a bigger building.
- **Level 2** is about **one to two days** of one builder on the day shift; two builders halve it.
- **Level 3** is about **three to five days** of one builder.

The build menu shows the time for two typical builders of your colony, and the Upgrade tab shows it for the next level. While a site is going, its panel shows the time left at the crew's pace, or why it stands still (paused, nobody on it).

## Tips

- An upgrade does not stop the building: keep its workers on.
- Put your best builders on long upgrades; the Construction skill grows as they build.
- Night shifts (an upgrade of a lit building) and more builders speed it up; dust storms stop it.
